sentences.zh: 始祖以下諸子

translations.literal: The various sons below the Founding Ancestor
translations.idiomatic: Sons and Descendants of the Founding Ancestor

sentences.zh: 勗，字勉道。

translations.literal: Xu, style name Miandao.
translations.idiomatic: Xu, whose style name was Miandao.

sentences.zh: 本名烏野，穆宗第五子。

translations.literal: Original name Wuye; fifth son of Emperor Muzong.
translations.idiomatic: Born Wuye, he was the fifth son of Emperor Muzong.

sentences.zh: 好學問，國人呼為秀才。

translations.literal: He loved learning; the people of the state called him Xiucai [the scholar].
translations.idiomatic: Fond of learning, his countrymen called him "the scholar."

sentences.zh: 年十六，從太祖攻甯江州，從宗望襲遼主于石輦鐸。

translations.literal: At age sixteen he followed Taizu in attacking Ningjiang Prefecture, and followed Zongwang in striking the Liao ruler at Shilian Duo.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen he followed Emperor Taizu in the assault on Ningjiang Prefecture and joined Zongwang in the surprise attack on the Liao emperor at Shilian Duo.

sentences.zh: 太宗嗣位，自軍中召還，與謀政事。

translations.literal: When Taizong succeeded to the throne, he was recalled from the army to deliberate on state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong took the throne, Xu was recalled from the field and brought into counsel on government.

sentences.zh: 宗翰、宗望定汴州，受宋帝降。

translations.literal: Zonghan and Zongwang secured Bianzhou and received the Song emperor's surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Zonghan and Zongwang took Bianzhou and accepted the surrender of the Song emperor.

sentences.zh: 太宗使勗就軍中往勞之。

translations.literal: Taizong sent Xu to the army to go and congratulate them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong sent Xu to the army to convey the court's congratulations.

sentences.zh: 宗翰等問其所欲。

translations.literal: Zonghan and the others asked what he desired.
translations.idiomatic: Zonghan and the others asked what reward he wanted.

sentences.zh: 曰：「惟好書耳。」

translations.literal: He said: "I only love books."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Books are all I care for."

sentences.zh: 載數車而還。

translations.literal: He loaded several cartloads and returned.
translations.idiomatic: They loaded several cartloads of books for him, and he returned home.

sentences.zh: 女直初無文字，及破遼，獲契丹、漢人，始通契丹、漢字，於是諸子皆學之。

translations.literal: The Jurchen at first had no writing; after defeating the Liao and capturing Khitan and Han people, they first gained access to Khitan and Han script, and then all the princes studied them.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchen had no writing of their own; after the conquest of Liao they took Khitan and Han captives and first learned Khitan and Chinese script, and the imperial sons all took up the study.

sentences.zh: 宗雄能以兩月盡通契丹大小字，而完顏希尹乃依仿契丹字制女直字。

translations.literal: Zongxiong could master both large and small Khitan script within two months, while Wanyan Xiyin modeled Jurchen characters on the Khitan script.
translations.idiomatic: Zongxiong mastered the full Khitan script in two months, while Wanyan Xiyin devised Jurchen characters modeled on the Khitan writing.

sentences.zh: 女直既未有文字，亦未嘗有記錄，故祖宗事皆不載。

translations.literal: Since the Jurchen had not yet had writing and had never kept records, affairs of the forefathers were nowhere written down.
translations.idiomatic: Because the Jurchen had no written language and no tradition of record-keeping, the deeds of the ancestors went unrecorded.

sentences.zh: 宗翰好訪問女直老人，多得祖宗遺事。

translations.literal: Zonghan liked to inquire of elderly Jurchen and obtained much of the forefathers' leftover lore.
translations.idiomatic: Zonghan made a habit of questioning elderly Jurchen and gathered many stories handed down about the ancestors.

sentences.zh: 太宗初即位，複進士舉，而韓昉輩皆在朝廷，文學之士稍拔擢用之。

translations.literal: When Taizong first took the throne, the jinshi examination was restored; Han Fang and his circle were all at court, and men of letters were gradually selected and employed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after Emperor Taizong's accession the jinshi civil examination was revived; Han Fang and others were already at court, and literary men began to be promoted into office.

sentences.zh: 天會六年，詔書求訪祖宗遺事，以備國史，命勗與耶律迪越掌之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianhui an edict sought out leftover lore of the ancestors to supply the national history, appointing Xu and Yelü Diyue to oversee it.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Tianhui (1128) an edict ordered a search for ancestral traditions to furnish the national history, with Xu and Yelü Diyue placed in charge.

sentences.zh: 勗等采摭遺言舊事，自始祖以下十帝，綜為三卷。

translations.literal: Xu and the others gathered stray sayings and old affairs from the ten emperors from the Founding Ancestor downward and compiled them into three scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Xu and his colleagues collected oral traditions and old accounts for the ten reigns from the Founding Ancestor onward and compiled them in three scrolls.

sentences.zh: 凡部族，既曰某部，複曰某水之某，又曰某鄉某村，以別識之。

translations.literal: For every tribal group they would say a certain tribe, also a certain place on a certain river, and again a certain hamlet or village, to distinguish and identify them.
translations.idiomatic: For each clan they noted the tribal name, then the branch on a given river, then the hamlet or village, so that each group could be told apart.

sentences.zh: 凡與契丹往來及征伐諸部，其間詐謀詭計，一無所隱。

translations.literal: All dealings with the Khitan and campaigns against the various tribes — the stratagems and ruses in between — were concealed in nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Their dealings with the Khitan and campaigns against the various tribes, including every stratagem and ruse, were set down without concealment.

sentences.zh: 事有詳有略，咸得其實。

translations.literal: Some matters were treated in detail and some in summary, but all obtained the truth.
translations.idiomatic: Some episodes were treated at length and others briefly, but in each case the truth was preserved.

sentences.zh: 自太祖與高麗議和，凡女直入高麗者皆索之，至十餘年，索之不已。

translations.literal: Since Taizu made peace with Goryeo, every Jurchen who had entered Goryeo was demanded back; for more than ten years the demands did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Taizu concluded peace with Goryeo, the court demanded the return of every Jurchen who had fled there — a claim pressed without pause for more than ten years.

sentences.zh: 勗上書諫曰：「臣聞德莫大于樂天，仁莫先于惠下。

translations.literal: Xu submitted a memorial of remonstrance, saying: "Your servant has heard that no virtue is greater than rejoicing in Heaven's mandate, and no benevolence comes before showing kindness to those below.
translations.idiomatic: Xu submitted a memorial of remonstrance: "I have heard that the greatest virtue is to rejoice in Heaven's will, and the foremost benevolence is to show kindness to one's subjects.

sentences.zh: 所索戶口，皆前世奸宄叛亡，烏蠢、訛謨罕、阿海、阿合束之緒裔。

translations.literal: The households demanded are all descendants of past traitors and fugitives — the lines of Wuchun, Emohan, Ahai, and Aheshu.
translations.idiomatic: The households now demanded are descendants of traitors and fugitives of earlier generations — the lines of Wuchun, Emohan, Ahai, and Aheshu.

sentences.zh: 先世綏懷四境，尚未賓服，自先君在與高麗通，聞我將大，因謂本自同出，稍稍款附。

translations.literal: In former generations the four borders were soothed but not yet fully submissive; since the former lord was in contact with Goryeo, hearing that we would grow great, they said we sprang from the same source and gradually drew near in goodwill.
translations.idiomatic: In earlier reigns the four borders had been pacified but not yet fully brought to allegiance; once our late sovereign opened relations with Goryeo, they heard that our state was rising and, claiming a common origin, began to draw near.

sentences.zh: 高麗既不聽許，遂生邊釁，因致交兵，久方連和，蓋三十年。

translations.literal: Goryeo would not consent, and border incidents arose, leading to war; only after a long time was peace restored — roughly thirty years.
translations.idiomatic: When Goryeo refused, border clashes followed and war broke out; peace was restored only after a long interval — some thirty years in all.

sentences.zh: 當時壯者今皆物故，子孫安於土俗，婚姻膠固，征索不已，彼固不敢稽留，骨肉乖離，誠非眾願。

translations.literal: The strong men of that time are all dead; their descendants are settled in local custom, marriages are firmly bound, yet the levies continue without end. They dare not detain them, yet kin are torn apart — this is truly not the wish of the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: The adults of that generation are all gone; their descendants have settled into local ways and formed lasting marriages, yet the demands go on. Goryeo does not dare withhold them, but families are torn apart — surely not what anyone wishes.

sentences.zh: 人情怨甚可湣者，而必欲求為己有，特彼我之蔽，非一視同仁之大也。

translations.literal: Human feeling is full of grievance and deeply pitiable, yet we insist on claiming them as our own — this is merely the blindness of "us" and "them," not the greatness of treating all alike.
translations.idiomatic: The resentment is pitiable, yet we insist on claiming them as ours — this is the narrow sight of "us" versus "them," not the magnanimity of treating all subjects alike.

sentences.zh: 國家民物繁夥，幅員萬里，不知得此果何益耶。

translations.literal: The state's people and goods are numerous, its territory ten thousand li — who knows what profit there is in gaining this?
translations.idiomatic: Our state already teems with people and goods across a realm of ten thousand li — what real gain could these few households bring?

sentences.zh: 今索之不還，我以強兵勁卒取之無難。

translations.literal: If they are demanded now and not returned, our strong troops and crack soldiers could take them without difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: If they are not returned now, our strong armies could seize them without difficulty.

sentences.zh: 然兵兇器，戰危事，不得已而後用。

translations.literal: Yet arms are an inauspicious instrument and battle a perilous affair — they are used only when there is no alternative.
translations.idiomatic: Yet arms are inauspicious tools and war a perilous undertaking, to be used only when there is no choice.

sentences.zh: 高麗稱籓，職貢不闕，國且臣屬，民亦非外。

translations.literal: Goryeo has declared itself a vassal; tribute duties are not lacking; the state is already subordinate, and the people are not outsiders.
translations.idiomatic: Goryeo has submitted as a vassal, tribute never lapses, the state is already our subject, and its people are not foreigners.

sentences.zh: 聖人行義，不責小過，理之所在，不俟終日。

translations.literal: The sage practices righteousness and does not censure small faults; where principle lies, he does not wait until the day's end.
translations.idiomatic: A sage ruler practices righteousness and does not harp on small faults; where principle points, he need not wait even a day.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為宜施惠下之仁，弘樂天之德，聽免征索，則彼不謂己有，如自我得之矣。」

translations.literal: Your servant foolishly thinks we should apply the benevolence of showing kindness below and enlarge the virtue of rejoicing in Heaven, and permit exemption from these levies; then they will not regard them as their own, but as if obtained from themselves."
translations.idiomatic: I humbly believe Your Majesty should extend kindness to your subjects and embody the virtue of rejoicing in Heaven's will by exempting these households from further demands; Goryeo will then feel as though it had gained them by its own grace, not lost them to force."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 十五年，為尚書左丞加鎮東軍節度使、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he became Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, with the additional titles of Military Commissioner of the Zhendong Army and Associate Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year (1137) he was appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, with concurrent posts as Military Commissioner of the Zhendong Army and Associate Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 預平宗磐之難，賜與甚多，加儀同三司，以「皇叔祖」字冠其銜。

translations.literal: Having taken part in quelling Zongpan's rebellion, he received many gifts; he was given the rank of Palace Attendant of the First Class, and the characters "Imperial Uncle-Grandfather" were placed at the head of his title.
translations.idiomatic: For his role in suppressing Zongpan's rebellion he received lavish rewards, was raised to Palace Attendant of the First Class, and had the honorific "Imperial Uncle-Grandfather" prefixed to his title.

sentences.zh: 勗皆力辭不受。

translations.literal: Xu strenuously declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Xu firmly declined every honor.

sentences.zh: 皇統元年，撰定熙宗尊號冊文。

translations.literal: In the first year of Huangtong he drafted the text of the honorific title for Emperor Xizong.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Huangtong (1141) he drafted the text proclaiming Emperor Xizong's honorific title.

sentences.zh: 上召勗飲於便殿，以玉帶賜之。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Xu to drink in the side hall and bestowed a jade belt on him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Xu to drink with him in the side hall and presented him with a jade belt.

sentences.zh: 所撰《祖宗實錄》成，凡三卷，進入，上焚香立受之，賞賚有差。

translations.literal: The Veritable Records of the Ancestors he had compiled was finished — three scrolls in all — and presented; the emperor burned incense and received it standing; rewards were graded accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: When his Veritable Records of the Ancestors was complete in three scrolls and presented, the emperor burned incense and received it standing; rewards were granted in due measure.

sentences.zh: 制詔左丞勗、平章政事弈職俸外別給二品親王俸傔。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that beyond their official salaries, Left Vice Director Xu and Director of the Secretariat Yi should each receive the salary and retinue of a second-rank imperial prince.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted Left Vice Director Xu and Director Yi, beyond their regular salaries, the stipend and retinue of a second-rank imperial prince.

sentences.zh: 舊制，皇兄弟、皇子為親王給二品俸。

translations.literal: By old regulation, imperial brothers and sons made princes received second-rank salaries.
translations.idiomatic: By established rule, imperial brothers and sons enfeoffed as princes received second-rank stipends.

sentences.zh: 宗室封一字王者給三品俸，勗等別給親王俸，皆異數也。

translations.literal: Members of the imperial clan enfeoffed as kings with a single-character title received third-rank salaries; Xu and the others were separately given princely salaries — all extraordinary favors.
translations.idiomatic: Clan members enfeoffed as kings with a single-character title received third-rank stipends; Xu and the others were separately granted princely stipends — all extraordinary favors.

sentences.zh: 宴群臣于五雲樓，勗進酒稱謝。

translations.literal: The emperor feasted the ministers at the Five Clouds Tower; Xu advanced wine and offered thanks.
translations.idiomatic: At a feast for the ministers in the Five Clouds Tower, Xu offered wine and expressed his thanks.

sentences.zh: 帝起立，宰臣進曰：「至尊為臣下屢起，于禮未安。」

translations.literal: The emperor rose to his feet; the chief ministers advanced and said: "Your Majesty repeatedly rises for your subjects — this is not proper in ritual."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rose to his feet; the chief ministers stepped forward and said, "Your Majesty rises again and again for your subjects — this is not proper by ritual."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「朕屈己待臣下，亦何害。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I humble myself in treating my subjects — what harm is there?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "What harm is there if I humble myself before my ministers?"

sentences.zh: 是日，上及群臣盡歡。

translations.literal: That day the emperor and the ministers enjoyed themselves to the full.
translations.idiomatic: That day the emperor and his ministers feasted in full merriment.

sentences.zh: 俄同監修國史，進拜平章政事。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he became co-supervisor of the compilation of the national history and was promoted to Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was made co-supervisor of the national history and promoted to Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 光懿皇后忌辰，熙宗將出獵，勗諫而止。

translations.literal: On the anniversary of Empress Guangyi's death, Xizong was about to go hunting; Xu remonstrated and he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: On the anniversary of Empress Guangyi's death, when Emperor Xizong was about to go hunting, Xu remonstrated and the hunt was canceled.

sentences.zh: 熙宗獵於海島，三日之間，親射五虎獲之。

translations.literal: Xizong hunted on the sea island; within three days he personally shot five tigers and took them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xizong hunted on a coastal island and within three days personally shot five tigers.

sentences.zh: 勗獻《東狩射虎賦》，上悅，賜以佩刀、玉帶、良馬。

translations.literal: Xu presented the "Rhapsody on the Eastern Hunt and Tiger Shooting"; the emperor was pleased and bestowed a girdle sword, jade belt, and fine horses.
translations.idiomatic: Xu presented his "Rhapsody on the Eastern Hunt and Tiger Shooting"; the emperor was pleased and rewarded him with a girdle sword, jade belt, and fine horses.

sentences.zh: 能以契丹字為詩文，凡遊宴有可言者，輒作詩以見意。

translations.literal: He could compose poetry and prose in Khitan script; whenever there was something worth saying at banquets or outings, he would compose a poem to express his meaning.
translations.idiomatic: He could compose poetry and prose in Khitan script; whenever a banquet or outing offered occasion for comment, he would write a poem to make his meaning known.

sentences.zh: 時上日與近臣酣飲，或繼以夜，莫能諫之。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor daily drank deeply with close ministers, sometimes continuing through the night; no one could remonstrate with him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the emperor drank heavily with his close ministers day after day, sometimes far into the night, and no one could bring him to stop.

sentences.zh: 勗上疏諫，乃為止酒。

translations.literal: Xu submitted a memorial of remonstrance, and only then did he cease drinking.
translations.idiomatic: Xu submitted a memorial of remonstrance, and only then did the emperor give up his excess.

sentences.zh: 進拜左丞相，兼侍中、監修如故。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Left Director of the Secretariat, retaining his concurrent posts as Palace Attendant and supervisor of compilation.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Left Director of the Secretariat while retaining his posts as Palace Attendant and supervisor of compilation.

sentences.zh: 八年，奏上《太祖實錄》二十卷，賜黃金八十兩，銀百兩，重彩五十端，絹百匹，通犀、玉鉤帶各一。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he presented the twenty-scroll Veritable Records of Taizu; he was granted eighty taels of gold, one hundred taels of silver, fifty bolts of heavy-colored silk, one hundred bolts of plain silk, and one each of rhinoceros horn and jade hook belts.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year (1148) he presented the twenty-scroll Veritable Records of Taizu and received eighty taels of gold, one hundred taels of silver, fifty bolts of heavy-colored silk, one hundred bolts of plain silk, and one rhinoceros-horn belt and one jade-hook belt.

sentences.zh: 出領行台尚書省事，召拜太保，領三省、領行台如故，封魯國王。

translations.literal: He went out to head the Branch Secretariat affairs, was summoned and appointed Grand Mentor, retained charge of the Three Departments and the Branch Secretariat as before, and was enfeoffed as King of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out to head Branch Secretariat affairs, then recalled and appointed Grand Mentor, retaining charge of the Three Departments and the Branch Secretariat, and enfeoffed as King of Lu.

sentences.zh: 勗剛正寡言。

translations.literal: Xu was upright and stern and spoke little.
translations.idiomatic: Xu was upright and stern, and spoke little.

sentences.zh: 海陵方用事，朝臣多附之者。

translations.literal: Hailing was just then rising in power, and many court officials attached themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Hailing was just then rising in power, and many court officials were attaching themselves to him.

sentences.zh: 一日，大臣會議，海陵後至，勗面責之曰：

translations.literal: One day the great ministers met in council; Hailing arrived late; Xu rebuked him to his face, saying:
translations.idiomatic: One day at a council of great ministers Hailing arrived late; Xu rebuked him to his face:

sentences.zh: 「吾年五十餘，猶不敢後，爾少年強健，肪敢如此。」

translations.literal: "I am over fifty and still dare not come late; you are young and strong — how dare you act like this?"
translations.idiomatic: "I am past fifty and still would not dare arrive late; you are young and fit — how dare you behave so?"

sentences.zh: 海陵跪謝。

translations.literal: Hailing knelt and apologized.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing knelt and apologized.

sentences.zh: 九年，進拜太師，進封漢國王。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was promoted to Grand Preceptor and advanced to King of Han.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year (1149) he was promoted to Grand Preceptor and advanced to King of Han.

sentences.zh: 海陵篡立，加恩大臣以收人望，封秦漢國王，領三省、監修如故。

translations.literal: When Hailing usurped the throne, he showed favor to great ministers to win public esteem; Xu was enfeoffed as King of Qin and Han, retaining charge of the Three Departments and supervision of compilation as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Hailing seized the throne he lavished honors on senior ministers to win public esteem; Xu was enfeoffed as King of Qin and Han, retaining charge of the Three Departments and supervision of compilation.

sentences.zh: 撰定《女直郡望姓氏譜》及他文甚眾。

translations.literal: He compiled the Genealogy of Jurchen Clan Prestige and Surnames and many other writings.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled the Genealogy of Jurchen Clan Prestige and Surnames and many other works besides.

sentences.zh: 大定二十年，詔曰：「太師勗諫表詩文甚有典則，朕自即位所未嘗見。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Dading an edict said: "Grand Preceptor Xu's memorials, remonstrances, and poems are full of classical norms; since Our accession We have never seen their like.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year of Dading (1180) an edict declared: "Grand Preceptor Xu's memorials of remonstrance and his poems are models of classical propriety; since Our accession We have seen nothing like them.

sentences.zh: 其諫表可入《實錄》，其《射虎賦》詩文等篇什，可鏤版持之。」

translations.literal: His remonstrance memorials may enter the Veritable Records; his "Rhapsody on Tiger Shooting," poems, and other pieces may be carved on blocks and preserved."
translations.idiomatic: His remonstrance memorials should enter the Veritable Records; his "Rhapsody on Tiger Shooting," poems, and other pieces should be carved on blocks for preservation."

sentences.zh: 子宗秀。

translations.literal: His son was Zongxiu.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Zongxiu.

sentences.zh: 子 宗秀

translations.literal: Son: Zongxiu
translations.idiomatic: Son: Zongxiu

sentences.zh: 宗秀，字實甫，本名撕里忽。

translations.literal: Zongxiu, style name Shifu, original name Silihu.
translations.idiomatic: Zongxiu, whose style name was Shifu, was born Silihu.

sentences.zh: 涉獵經史，通契丹大小字。

translations.literal: He ranged widely through the classics and histories and mastered both large and small Khitan script.
translations.idiomatic: He read widely in the classics and histories and mastered the full Khitan script.

sentences.zh: 善騎射，與平宗磐、宗雋之亂，授定遠大將軍，以宗磐世襲猛安授之。

translations.literal: Skilled in horsemanship and archery, he took part in quelling the rebellions of Zongpan and Zongjun; he was appointed General Who Pacifies the Far Reaches, and Zongpan's hereditary meng'an was granted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled in horsemanship and archery, he helped suppress the rebellions of Zongpan and Zongjun and was appointed General Who Pacifies the Far Reaches, with Zongpan's hereditary meng'an granted to him.

sentences.zh: 宗弼複取河南，宗秀與海陵俱赴軍前任使。

translations.literal: When Zongbi retook Henan, Zongxiu and Hailing both went to the army to take up assignments.
translations.idiomatic: When Zongbi retook Henan, Zongxiu and Prince Hailing both went to the army on assignment.

sentences.zh: 宋將岳飛軍於亳、宿之間，宗秀率步騎三千扼其沖要，遂與諸軍逆擊敗之。

translations.literal: The Song general Yue Fei's army was between Bo and Su; Zongxiu led three thousand infantry and cavalry to hold the strategic choke point, then with the other armies struck back and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song general Yue Fei camped between Bo and Su prefectures, Zongxiu led three thousand foot and horse to hold the strategic pass and, joining the other armies, counterattacked and routed him.

sentences.zh: 師還，為太原尹，改婆速路統軍使、不受。

translations.literal: When the army returned he became Prefect of Taiyuan; he was reassigned as Military Commissioner of the Basu Circuit but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: After the campaign he was made Prefect of Taiyuan; when offered the post of Military Commissioner of the Basu Circuit he declined.

sentences.zh: 高麗遣使以士產獻，卻之。

translations.literal: Goryeo sent envoys presenting local products; he declined them.
translations.idiomatic: When Goryeo sent envoys bearing local products as gifts, he refused them.

sentences.zh: 入為刑部尚書，改禦史中丞，授翰林學士。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Director of the Ministry of Justice, was changed to Vice Censor-in-Chief, and appointed Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to the capital, he served as Director of the Ministry of Justice, then Vice Censor-in-Chief, and was appointed Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 天德初，轉承旨，封宿國公，賜玉帶。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tiande he was transferred to Chief Academician, enfeoffed as Duke of Su, and granted a jade belt.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Tiande era (1135) he was made Chief Academician, enfeoffed as Duke of Su, and granted a jade belt.

sentences.zh: 曆平陽尹、昭義軍節度使，封廣平郡王。

translations.literal: He served successively as Prefect of Pingyang and Military Commissioner of the Zhaoyi Army, and was enfeoffed as Prince of Guangping Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Prefect of Pingyang and Military Commissioner of the Zhaoyi Army and was enfeoffed as Prince of Guangping.

sentences.zh: 正隆二年卒官，年四十二。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenglong he died in office at age forty-two.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhenglong (1157) he died in office at the age of forty-two.

sentences.zh: 是歲，例降二品以上封爵，改贈金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: That year, by regulation titles of the second rank and above were reduced; he was posthumously given Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Blue Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: That year, when enfeoffments of the second rank and above were reduced by regulation, he was posthumously granted the title Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Blue Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 康宗敬僖皇后生楚王謀良虎。

translations.literal: Emperor Kangzong's Empress Jingyi bore the Prince of Chu, Moulianghu.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Kangzong's Empress Jingyi bore the Prince of Chu, Moulianghu.

sentences.zh: 次室溫都氏生昭武大將軍同喬茁。

translations.literal: A secondary consort of the Wendu clan bore General of Illustrious Martiality Tong Qiaozhuo.
translations.idiomatic: A secondary consort of the Wendu clan bore General of Illustrious Martiality Tong Qiaozhuo.

sentences.zh: 次室僕散氏坐事早死，生龍虎衛上將軍隈可。

translations.literal: A secondary consort of the Pusan clan, implicated in a case, died early; she bore General-in-Chief of the Dragon-Tiger Guard Wei Ke.
translations.idiomatic: A secondary consort of the Pusan clan, implicated in a case, died young; she bore General-in-Chief of the Dragon-Tiger Guard Wei Ke.

sentences.zh: 始祖兄弟三人，保活里之後為神士懣、迪古乃，別有傳。

translations.literal: The Founding Ancestor had three brothers; the descendants of Baohuoli were Shenshimen and Digunai — each has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Ancestor had three brothers; the line of Baohuoli produced Shenshimen and Digunai, each treated in a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 胡十門

translations.literal: Hu Shimen
translations.idiomatic: Hu Shimen

sentences.zh: 胡十門者，曷蘇館人也。

translations.literal: Hu Shimen was a man of the Hesuguan [Yehü clan settlement].
translations.idiomatic: Hu Shimen was a man of the Hesuguan settlement.

sentences.zh: 父撻不野，事遼為太尉。

translations.literal: His father Tabuye served the Liao as Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tabuye had served the Liao as Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 胡十門善漢語，通契丹大小字，勇而善戰。

translations.literal: Hu Shimen was skilled in Chinese, mastered both large and small Khitan script, and was brave and adept in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Shimen was fluent in Chinese, mastered the full Khitan script, and was both brave and skilled in battle.

sentences.zh: 高永昌據東京，招曷蘇館人，眾畏高永昌兵強，且欲歸之。

translations.literal: Gao Yongchang held Dongjing [Liaoyang] and summoned the Hesuguan people; the multitude feared Gao Yongchang's strong troops and also wished to submit to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Yongchang seized Dongjing (Liaoyang) and summoned the Hesuguan people, many feared his strong forces and were inclined to join him.

sentences.zh: 胡十門不肯從，召其族人謀曰：「吾遠祖兄弟三人，同出高麗。

translations.literal: Hu Shimen would not follow; he summoned his clansmen to deliberate, saying: "Our remote ancestors were three brothers who all came forth from Goryeo.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Shimen refused. He summoned his clansmen and said, "Our remote ancestors were three brothers who all came from Goryeo.

sentences.zh: 今大聖皇帝之祖入女直，吾祖留高麗，自高麗歸於遼。

translations.literal: Now the Great Sage Emperor's ancestor entered the Jurchen; our ancestor remained in Goryeo and from Goryeo returned to the Liao.
translations.idiomatic: The ancestor of the Great Sage Emperor joined the Jurchen; our ancestor stayed in Goryeo and later came from Goryeo to serve the Liao.

sentences.zh: 吾與皇帝皆三祖之後。

translations.literal: The emperor and I are both descendants of the three ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor and I are both descendants of those three ancestors.

sentences.zh: 皇帝受命即大位，遼之敗亡有征，吾豈能為永昌之臣哉！」

translations.literal: The emperor received the mandate and took the great throne; the Liao's defeat and ruin have clear signs — how could I become Yongchang's subject!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor has received Heaven's mandate and taken the throne; the fall of Liao is already foretold — how could I become Yongchang's subject?"

sentences.zh: 始祖兄阿古乃留高麗中，胡十門自言如此，蓋自謂阿古乃之後雲。

translations.literal: The Founding Ancestor's elder brother Agunai remained in Goryeo; Hu Shimen spoke of himself in this way — presumably claiming to be a descendant of Agunai.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Ancestor's elder brother Agunai had remained in Goryeo; Hu Shimen spoke in this way because he considered himself a descendant of Agunai.

sentences.zh: 於是率其族屬部眾詣撒改，烏蠢降，營於馳回山之下。

translations.literal: Thereupon he led his clansmen and tribal followers to Sagai; Wuchun submitted, and they encamped below Mount Chihui.
translations.idiomatic: He then led his clan and followers to Sagai; when Wuchun submitted, they encamped below Mount Chihui.

sentences.zh: 永昌攻之，胡十門力戰不能敵，奔於撒改。

translations.literal: Yongchang attacked them; Hu Shimen fought fiercely but could not prevail and fled to Sagai.
translations.idiomatic: Yongchang attacked them; Hu Shimen fought hard but could not hold and fled to Sagai.

sentences.zh: 及攻開州，胡十門以糧餉給軍。

translations.literal: When they attacked Kaizhou, Hu Shimen supplied provisions to the army.
translations.idiomatic: During the assault on Kaizhou he supplied provisions to the army.

sentences.zh: 後攻保州，遼獎以舟師遁，胡十門邀擊敗之，降其士卒。

translations.literal: Later, when they attacked Baozhou, the Liao commander Jiang Yi fled by river with his fleet; Hu Shimen intercepted and defeated them and accepted the surrender of their soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Later, during the assault on Baozhou, the Liao commander Jiang Yi fled by river with his fleet; Hu Shimen intercepted and routed them and accepted the surrender of their troops.

sentences.zh: 賞賜甚厚，以為曷蘇館七部勃堇，給銀牌一、木牌三。

translations.literal: Rewards were very generous; he was made bojin of the seven tribes of Hesuguan and given one silver tablet and three wooden tablets.
translations.idiomatic: He received lavish rewards and was appointed bojin over the seven tribes of Hesuguan, with one silver tablet and three wooden tablets granted him.

sentences.zh: 天輔二年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the second year of Tianfu.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Tianfu (1118).

sentences.zh: 贈監門衛上將軍，再贈驃騎衛上將軍。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given General-in-Chief of the Gate Guards, and later again General-in-Chief of the Valiant Cavalry Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the title General-in-Chief of the Gate Guards, and later advanced to General-in-Chief of the Valiant Cavalry Guard.

sentences.zh: 子鉤室，嘗從攻顯州，領四謀克軍，破梁魚務，功最，以其父所管七部為曷蘇館都勃堇。

translations.literal: His son Goushi had followed in the attack on Xianzhou, leading four meng'an armies, defeating Liang Yuwu with the greatest merit; the seven tribes his father had governed were made the chief bojin of Hesuguan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Goushi had taken part in the assault on Xianzhou at the head of four meng'an armies, routed Liang Yuwu with the greatest distinction, and was made chief bojin of Hesuguan over the seven tribes his father had governed.

sentences.zh: 有合住者，亦稱始祖兄苗裔，但不知與胡十門相去幾從耳。

translations.literal: There was also Hezhu, who likewise claimed to be a descendant of the Founding Ancestor's elder brother, but it is not known how many generations removed he was from Hu Shimen.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Hezhu, who likewise claimed descent from the Founding Ancestor's elder brother, though how many generations separated him from Hu Shimen is unknown.

sentences.zh: 合住，曷速館苾里海水人也。

translations.literal: Hezhu was a man of the Bilihai River in Hesuguan.
translations.idiomatic: Hezhu was from the Bilihai River district of the Hesuguan settlement.

sentences.zh: 仕遼，領辰、複二州漢人、渤海。

translations.literal: He served the Liao and oversaw the Han and Bohai populations of Chen and Fu prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He had served the Liao, overseeing the Han and Bohai populations of Chen and Fu prefectures.

sentences.zh: 曾孙 布輝

translations.literal: Great-grandson: Buhui
translations.idiomatic: Great-grandson: Buhui

sentences.zh: 子蒲速越，襲父職，再遷靜江中正軍節度使，佩金牌，為曷速館女直部長。

translations.literal: His son Pusuyue inherited his father's post, was twice transferred to Military Commissioner of the Jingjiang Zhongzheng Army, wore a gold tablet, and was chief of the Jurchen tribes of Hesuguan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Pusuyue inherited his father's post, was twice promoted to Military Commissioner of the Jingjiang Zhongzheng Army, wore a gold tablet, and served as chief of the Jurchen tribes of Hesuguan.

sentences.zh: 子余里也與胡十門同時歸朝，屢以糧餉助伐高永昌及高麗、新羅。

translations.literal: His son Yuliye submitted to the court at the same time as Hu Shimen and repeatedly supplied provisions to aid campaigns against Gao Yongchang, Goryeo, and Silla.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuliye submitted to the court at the same time as Hu Shimen and repeatedly supplied provisions for campaigns against Gao Yongchang, Goryeo, and Silla.

sentences.zh: 後從宗望伐宋，以功遷真定府路安撫使兼曹州防禦使，佩金牌。

translations.literal: Later he followed Zongwang in the campaign against Song and, for merit, was transferred to Pacification Commissioner of the Zhending Circuit and concurrently Defense Commissioner of Cao Prefecture, wearing a gold tablet.
translations.idiomatic: He later followed Zongwang in the campaign against Song and, for his service, was appointed Pacification Commissioner of the Zhending Circuit with concurrent post as Defense Commissioner of Cao Prefecture and a gold tablet.

sentences.zh: 授苾里海水世襲猛安。

translations.literal: He was granted the hereditary meng'an of the Bilihai River.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted the hereditary meng'an of the Bilihai River district.

sentences.zh: 長子布輝，識女直、契丹、漢字，善騎射。

translations.literal: The eldest son Buhui knew Jurchen, Khitan, and Han script and was skilled in horsemanship and archery.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest son Buhui was literate in Jurchen, Khitan, and Chinese script and skilled in horsemanship and archery.

sentences.zh: 年十八，宗弼選為紮也，從阿里、蒲盧渾追宋康王於明州。

translations.literal: At age eighteen Zongbi selected him as zhaye and he followed Ali and Puluhun in pursuing the Song Prince of Kang at Mingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen Zongbi selected him as a zhaye scout and he joined Ali and Puluhun in pursuing the Song Prince of Kang at Mingzhou.

sentences.zh: 睿宗聞其才，召置麾下，從經略山東、河北、陝西，襲其父猛安，授昭勇大將軍。

translations.literal: Prince Ruizong heard of his talent and summoned him to his staff; he followed in securing Shandong, Hebei, and Shaanxi, inherited his father's meng'an, and was appointed General of Manifest Courage.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ruizong heard of his ability and took him onto his staff; he served in the pacification of Shandong, Hebei, and Shaanxi, inherited his father's meng'an, and was appointed General of Manifest Courage.

sentences.zh: 海陵伐宋，以本猛安兵從，半道與南征萬戶完顏福壽等俱亡歸，謁世宗于遼陽。

translations.literal: When Hailing campaigned against Song he followed with his meng'an troops; halfway there he fled home with the Southern Campaign Commander Wanyan Fushou and others and presented himself to Emperor Shizong at Liaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Hailing campaigned against Song he marched with his meng'an troops, but halfway there he deserted with the Southern Campaign Commander Wanyan Fushou and others and presented himself to Emperor Shizong at Liaoyang.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，除同知曷蘇館節度使事。

translations.literal: When Shizong took the throne, he was appointed Associate Commissioner of the Hesuguan Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong took the throne, Buhui was appointed Associate Commissioner of the Hesuguan Military Commission.

sentences.zh: 刑部侍郎斜哥為都統，布輝副之，坐擅署置官吏、私用官中財物，削兩階解職。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice Xiege was made commander-in-chief with Buhui as his deputy; for unauthorized appointment of officials and private use of government property, he was demoted two ranks and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Xiege of the Ministry of Justice was made commander-in-chief with Buhui as deputy; for appointing officials without authorization and misusing government property, Buhui was demoted two ranks and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 未浹旬，世宗獻享山陵。

translations.literal: Within less than ten days Shizong offered sacrifices at the imperial tombs.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days Emperor Shizong went to offer sacrifices at the imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書可喜、昭毅大將軍斡論、中都同知完顏璋等謀反，欲因上謁山陵舉事。

translations.literal: Director of the Ministry of War Keqi, General of Resolute Martiality Wolun, Associate Prefect of the Central Capital Wanyan Zhang, and others plotted rebellion, intending to act when the emperor visited the tombs.
translations.idiomatic: Director Keqi of the Ministry of War, General of Resolute Martiality Wolun, Associate Prefect Wanyan Zhang of the Central Capital, and others plotted rebellion, planning to strike when the emperor visited the tombs.

sentences.zh: 斡論與布輝親舊，與之謀議，事具《可喜傳》。

translations.literal: Wolun was close to Buhui and deliberated with him; the affair is fully recorded in the biography of Keqi.
translations.idiomatic: Wolun was an old associate of Buhui and drew him into the plot; the full account appears in the biography of Keqi.

sentences.zh: 既知事不可成，乃與可喜、璋執斡論等上變。

translations.literal: When they knew the affair could not succeed, they joined Keqi and Zhang in arresting Wolun and the others and reporting the plot.
translations.idiomatic: Realizing the plot could not succeed, Buhui joined Keqi and Zhang in arresting Wolun and the others and reporting the conspiracy.

sentences.zh: 可喜不肯以始謀盡首，遂並誅之，而賞布輝、璋。

translations.literal: Keqi would not fully confess his initial plotting, and so all were executed; Buhui and Zhang were rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: Keqi refused to confess his full role in the plot and was executed along with the others; Buhui and Zhang were rewarded.

sentences.zh: 除布輝浚州防禦使，累遷順天軍節度使。

translations.literal: Buhui was appointed Defense Commissioner of Jun Prefecture and was successively promoted to Military Commissioner of the Shuntian Army.
translations.idiomatic: Buhui was appointed Defense Commissioner of Jun Prefecture and eventually rose to Military Commissioner of the Shuntian Army.

sentences.zh: 致仕，卒，年六十七。

translations.literal: He retired and died at age sixty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He retired from office and died at the age of sixty-seven.

sentences.zh: 昭祖族人摑保者，從昭祖耀武於青嶺、白山。

translations.literal: Guai Bao of the Zhao Ancestor's clan followed the Zhao Ancestor in displaying martial prowess at the Green Ridge and White Mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Guai Bao, a clansman of the Zhao Ancestor, accompanied him in displaying martial prowess at the Green Ridge and White Mountains.

sentences.zh: 還至姑里甸，昭祖得疾，寢於村舍，洞無門扉，乃以車輪當門為蔽，摑保臥輪下為捍禦。

translations.literal: Returning to Guli Field, the Zhao Ancestor fell ill and lay in a village hut; the cave had no door, so they used a cart wheel to block the entrance, and Guai Bao lay beneath the wheel as a shield.
translations.idiomatic: On the return to Guli Field the Zhao Ancestor fell ill and rested in a village hut with no proper door; they blocked the entrance with a cart wheel, and Guai Bao lay beneath it as a guard.

sentences.zh: 已而賊至，刃交於輪輻間。

translations.literal: Before long bandits arrived, and blades clashed between the wheel spokes.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits soon arrived, and blades clashed between the wheel spokes.

sentences.zh: 摑保洞腹見膏，恐昭祖知之，乃然薪取膏以為炙，問之，以他肉對。

translations.literal: Guai Bao's belly was cut open and his fat exposed; fearing the Zhao Ancestor would know, he burned firewood to roast the fat as meat and, when asked, answered that it was other meat.
translations.idiomatic: Guai Bao's belly was laid open and his fat exposed; fearing the Zhao Ancestor would learn of it, he burned firewood to roast the fat as meat and, when questioned, said it was ordinary meat.

sentences.zh: 昭祖心知之，遂中夜啟行。

translations.literal: The Zhao Ancestor knew in his heart and set out at midnight.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhao Ancestor understood in his heart and set out at midnight.

sentences.zh: 衷，本名醜漢，中都司屬司人，世祖曾孫。

translations.literal: Zhong, original name Chouhan, was a man of the Directorate of Palace Services in the Central Capital and a great-grandson of Emperor Shizu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong, born Chouhan, was of the Directorate of Palace Services in the Central Capital and a great-grandson of Emperor Shizu.

sentences.zh: 祖霸合布里封鄆王，父悟烈官至特進。

translations.literal: His grandfather Bahebuli was enfeoffed as Prince of Yun; his father Wulie rose to Special Advancement.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Bahebuli was enfeoffed as Prince of Yun; his father Wulie rose to the rank of Special Advancement.

sentences.zh: 大定中，收充閤門祗候，授代州宣銳軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: During the Dading era he was enrolled as a gate attendant and appointed Commander of the Xuanrui Army in Dai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dading era he was enrolled as a gate attendant and appointed Commander of the Xuanrui Army in Dai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 歲旱，州委禱雨於五台靈潭，步致其水，雨隨下，人為刻石紀之。

translations.literal: In a year of drought the prefecture entrusted him to pray for rain at the Spirit Pool on Mount Wutai; he walked to bring back its water, rain followed, and the people carved a stone to record it.
translations.idiomatic: In a drought year the prefecture sent him to pray for rain at the Spirit Pool on Mount Wutai; he walked there to bring back its water, rain followed at once, and the people erected a stone to commemorate the event.

sentences.zh: 四遷引進使，兼典客署令，改尚輦局使。

translations.literal: He was transferred four times to Commissioner of Presentation, concurrently Director of the Bureau of Guests, then changed to Director of the Imperial Carriage Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted four times to Commissioner of Presentation, served concurrently as Director of the Bureau of Guests, and was then made Director of the Imperial Carriage Office.

sentences.zh: 扈從北幸，賜廄馬二以旌其勤。

translations.literal: Accompanying the northern tour, he was granted two stable horses to honor his diligence.
translations.idiomatic: On the emperor's northern tour he was rewarded with two stable horses in recognition of his diligence.

sentences.zh: 尋為夏國王李仁孝封冊使，曆寧海、蠡州刺史，入為大睦親府丞。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he became envoy to invest Li Renxiao, King of Western Xia; he served as Prefect of Ninghai and Li prefectures and entered the capital as Vice Director of the Bureau of Imperial Kinship.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed envoy to invest Li Renxiao, King of Western Xia, served as Prefect of Ninghai and Li prefectures, and was recalled as Vice Director of the Bureau of Imperial Kinship.

sentences.zh: 除順義軍節度使，陛辭，賜金幣，特寵異之。

translations.literal: He was appointed Military Commissioner of the Shunyi Army; at his farewell audience he was granted gold and coins and received special favor.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed Military Commissioner of the Shunyi Army, he received gold and coins at his farewell audience and was singled out for special favor.

sentences.zh: 移鎮鎮西。

translations.literal: He was transferred to command Zhenxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the Zhenxi command.

sentences.zh: 泰和六年，致仕，卒。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Taihe he retired and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Taihe (1206) he retired and died.

sentences.zh: 衷孝悌貞謹，深悉本朝婚禮，皇族婚嫁每令衷相之。

translations.literal: Zhong was filial, fraternal, upright, and careful, thoroughly versed in the marriage rites of the dynasty; for each imperial clan wedding and betrothal Zhong was ordered to oversee the arrangements.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong was filial, fraternal, upright, and careful, and thoroughly versed in the dynasty's marriage rites; imperial clan weddings were routinely entrusted to his oversight.

sentences.zh: 治複有能稱，其在寧海、蠡州，平賦役無擾，民立石頌遺愛。

translations.literal: In governance he likewise had a reputation for ability; at Ninghai and Li he kept taxes and corvée even without disturbance, and the people erected stones praising his lingering kindness.
translations.idiomatic: As an administrator he was likewise praised; at Ninghai and Li he kept taxes and corvée fair and unobtrusive, and the people erected stones in praise of his kindness.

sentences.zh: 大安初，追贈輔國上將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Da'an he was posthumously given General Who Assists the State.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Da'an era he was posthumously granted the title General Who Assists the State.

sentences.zh: 齊，本名掃合，穆宗曾孫。

translations.literal: Qi, original name Saohe, was a great-grandson of Emperor Muzong.
translations.idiomatic: Qi, born Saohe, was a great-grandson of Emperor Muzong.

sentences.zh: 父胡八魯，甯州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Hubalu was Prefect of Ning Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His father Hubalu had served as Prefect of Ning Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 大定中，以族次充司屬司將軍，授同知複州軍州事，累遷刑部員外郎。

translations.literal: During Dading, by clan seniority he filled the post of General of the Directorate of Palace Services, was appointed Associate Prefect of Fu Military Prefecture, and was successively promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dading era he filled the clan quota as General of the Directorate of Palace Services, was appointed Associate Prefect of Fu Military Prefecture, and rose to Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 上諭曰：「本朝以來，未嘗有內族為六部郎官者，以卿曆職廉能，故授之。」

translations.literal: The emperor instructed him: "Since this dynasty's founding there has never been a member of the inner clan as a bureau director in the Six Ministries; because you have served with integrity and ability, this post is granted you."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told him, "Since our dynasty's founding no member of the inner clan has held a bureau directorship in the Six Ministries; you are granted this post because of your integrity and ability in office."

sentences.zh: 先是，複州合廝罕關地方七百八里，因圍獵，禁民樵捕。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Hegesihan Pass in Fu Prefecture covered seven hundred and eighty li; because of hunting preserves, the people were forbidden to gather firewood or hunt.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Hegesihan Pass district in Fu Prefecture covered seven hundred and eighty li; as a hunting preserve, the people had been forbidden to gather firewood or hunt there.

sentences.zh: 齊言其地肥衍，令賦民開種則公私有益。

translations.literal: Qi said the land was fertile and broad; if the people were taxed to open it for cultivation, both public and private interests would benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Qi argued that the land was fertile and extensive and that allowing the people to open it for cultivation would benefit both state and populace.

sentences.zh: 上然之，為弛禁。

translations.literal: The emperor approved and relaxed the prohibition.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and lifted the ban.

sentences.zh: 即牧民以居，田收甚利，因名其地曰合廝罕猛安。

translations.literal: Herdsmen were immediately settled there; harvests were very profitable, and the place was therefore named the Hegesihan meng'an.
translations.idiomatic: Herdsmen were settled there at once; harvests proved highly profitable, and the district was named the Hegesihan meng'an.

sentences.zh: 章宗立，改戶部員外郎，出為磁州刺史，治以寬簡，未嘗留獄。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhangzong took the throne, he was changed to Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue and sent out as Prefect of Ci Prefecture; he governed with leniency and simplicity and never kept cases in detention.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhangzong took the throne, Qi was transferred to Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue and sent out as Prefect of Ci Prefecture, where he governed with leniency and simplicity and never held cases in detention.

sentences.zh: 屬邑武安，有道士視觀宇不謹，吏民為請鄰郡王師者代主之。

translations.literal: In the subordinate county of Wu'an a Daoist priest was negligent in tending the temple precinct; officials and people asked Wang Shi of the neighboring prefecture to take charge in his place.
translations.idiomatic: In the subordinate county of Wu'an a Daoist priest was negligent in tending the temple; officials and townspeople asked Wang Shi of the neighboring prefecture to take charge in his stead.

sentences.zh: 道士忿奪其利，告王私置禁銅器，法當徒。

translations.literal: The priest, resenting the loss of his profit, reported that Wang had privately set up forbidden bronze vessels — by law punishable by penal servitude.
translations.idiomatic: The priest, resenting the loss of his income, accused Wang of privately keeping forbidden bronze vessels — an offense punishable by penal servitude.

sentences.zh: 縣令惡其為人，反坐之，具獄上。

translations.literal: The county magistrate disliked Wang's character and turned the charge back on him, completing the case and sending it up.
translations.idiomatic: The county magistrate, disliking Wang's character, reversed the charge against him and forwarded the completed case.

sentences.zh: 齊審其誣。

translations.literal: Qi examined it and found it false.
translations.idiomatic: Qi reviewed the case and found it to be a fabrication.

sentences.zh: 又以王有德，不忍坐之，問同僚，無以對。

translations.literal: Moreover, because Wang had virtue, he could not bear to punish him; he asked his colleagues, and none could answer.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, because Wang was a man of virtue, Qi could not bear to punish him; he asked his colleagues, and none could suggest a solution.

sentences.zh: 齊曰：「道士同請即同居也，當准首，俱釋其罪。」

translations.literal: Qi said: "The priest jointly requested Wang's appointment, so they are cohabiting parties; the principal charge should apply, and both should be released from guilt."
translations.idiomatic: Qi said, "The priest jointly requested Wang's appointment, so they are cohabiting parties; apply the principal charge and release both from guilt."

sentences.zh: 其寬明有體，皆此類也。

translations.literal: His leniency, clarity, and sense of principle were all of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: His leniency, clarity, and sense of principle were all of this kind.

sentences.zh: 磁，名郡，刺史皆朝廷遴選，郡人以前政有聲如劉徽柔、程輝、高德裕皆不及也。

translations.literal: Ci was a renowned commandery whose prefects were all selected by the court; the people considered that earlier administrators of note such as Liu Huirou, Cheng Hui, and Gao Deyu did not equal him.
translations.idiomatic: Ci was a renowned commandery whose prefects were handpicked by the court; the people held that even celebrated predecessors such as Liu Huirou, Cheng Hui, and Gao Deyu did not match him.

sentences.zh: 河北提刑司以治狀聞。

translations.literal: The Hebei Judicial Commission reported his record of governance.
translations.idiomatic: The Hebei Judicial Commission reported his record of governance to the court.

sentences.zh: 明昌三年，始議置諸王傅，頗難其選，乃以齊傅袞王。

translations.literal: In the third year of Mingchang, when tutors for the imperial princes were first proposed, the selection was quite difficult, and Qi was made tutor to Prince Gun.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Mingchang (1192), when tutors for the imperial princes were first proposed, the choice proved difficult, and Qi was appointed tutor to Prince Gun.

sentences.zh: 王將至任郡，猛安迎接，齊峻卻之。

translations.literal: When the prince was about to reach his assigned prefecture, the meng'an commanders came out to welcome him; Qi sternly refused them.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince was about to reach his assigned prefecture, the meng'an commanders came out to welcome him; Qi sternly turned them away.

sentences.zh: 王怪問故，曰：「王國籓輔，猛安皆總戎職，于王何利焉，卻之以遠嫌也。」

translations.literal: The prince asked in surprise the reason; he said: "Your Highness is a feudal support to the realm; the meng'an commanders all hold military posts — what benefit is there for Your Highness? I refused them to keep suspicion at a distance."
translations.idiomatic: The prince asked the reason in surprise. Qi replied, "Your Highness is a feudal pillar of the realm; the meng'an commanders all hold military posts — what advantage could their welcome bring you? I turned them away to keep suspicion at a distance."

sentences.zh: 王悅服。

translations.literal: The prince was pleased and convinced.
translations.idiomatic: The prince was pleased and convinced.

sentences.zh: 王府家奴為不法，輒發還本猛安，終更無敢犯者。

translations.literal: When princely household slaves committed unlawful acts, he would send them back to their home meng'an; after his term none dared offend again.
translations.idiomatic: When princely household slaves broke the law, he sent them back to their home meng'an; after his term none dared offend again.

sentences.zh: 明年，授山東東、西路副統軍，兼同知益都府事。

translations.literal: The next year he was appointed Deputy Commander-in-Chief of the Eastern and Western Shandong Circuits and concurrently Associate Prefect of Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was appointed Deputy Commander-in-Chief of the Eastern and Western Shandong Circuits with concurrent post as Associate Prefect of Yidu.

sentences.zh: 有惠愛，郡人為之立碑。

translations.literal: He showed kindness and care; the people of the commandery erected a stele for him.
translations.idiomatic: He governed with kindness and care, and the people of the commandery erected a stele in his honor.

sentences.zh: 轉彰化軍節度使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Military Commissioner of the Zhanghua Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Military Commissioner of the Zhanghua Army.

sentences.zh: 六年，移利涉軍。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was moved to the Lishe Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was transferred to the Lishe Army command.

sentences.zh: 召見，勞尉有加。

translations.literal: He was summoned for an audience and received extra consolation and rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to court, he received special commendation and rewards.

sentences.zh: 詔留守上京。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him to remain and guard the Upper Capital.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed him to remain and guard the Upper Capital.

sentences.zh: 承安二年，致仕，卒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Cheng'an he retired and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Cheng'an (1197) he retired and died.

sentences.zh: 齊明法識治體，所至有聲，內族中與丞相承暉並稱雲。

translations.literal: Qi understood law and grasped the principles of governance; wherever he went he had a reputation; among the inner clan he was paired in renown with Chancellor Chenghui.
translations.idiomatic: Qi understood law and grasped the principles of governance; wherever he served he won renown; among the inner clan he was ranked alongside Chancellor Chenghui.

sentences.zh: 朮魯，宗室子。

translations.literal: Pailu, a son of the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: Pailu, a member of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 從鄭王斡賽敗高麗於曷懶，取亞魯城，克甯江州，取黃龍府。

translations.literal: He followed Prince Zheng Wosai in defeating Goryeo at Yalan, taking Yalu City, capturing Ningjiang Prefecture, and taking Huanglong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Prince Zheng Wosai in defeating Goryeo at Yalan, taking Yalu City, capturing Ningjiang Prefecture, and seizing Huanglong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 出河店之役、達魯古城之役、護步荅岡之役皆力戰有功。

translations.literal: At the battles of Chuhedian, Dalugu City, and Hubudagang he fought fiercely with merit.
translations.idiomatic: At the battles of Chuhedian, Dalugu City, and Hubudagang he fought fiercely and distinguished himself.

sentences.zh: 東京降，為本路招安副使。

translations.literal: When Dongjing surrendered, he became Deputy Pacification Commissioner of that circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When Dongjing (Liaoyang) surrendered, he was made Deputy Pacification Commissioner of that circuit.

sentences.zh: 敗遼兵，破同刮營。

translations.literal: He defeated Liao troops and destroyed the Tonggua camp.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated Liao troops and destroyed the Tonggua camp.

sentences.zh: 蘇州漢民叛走，朮魯追複之，以功為謀克。

translations.literal: Han people of Suzhou rebelled and fled; Pailu pursued and recovered them; for merit he was made a meng'an commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Han subjects of Suzhou rebelled and fled, Pailu pursued and recovered them and was made a meng'an commander for his service.

sentences.zh: 天輔四年卒，年四十一。

translations.literal: He died in the fourth year of Tianfu at age forty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year of Tianfu (1120) at the age of forty-one.

sentences.zh: 皇統中，贈鎮國上將軍。

translations.literal: During Huangtong he was posthumously given General Who Stabilizes the State.
translations.idiomatic: During the Huangtong era he was posthumously granted the title General Who Stabilizes the State.

sentences.zh: 胡石改

translations.literal: Hu Shigai
translations.idiomatic: Hu Shigai

sentences.zh: 胡石改，宗室子也。

translations.literal: Hu Shigai was a son of the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Shigai was a member of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 從太祖攻甯江，敗遼兵于達魯古城，破遼主親兵，皆有功。

translations.literal: He followed Taizu in attacking Ningjiang, defeated Liao troops at Dalugu City, and broke the Liao emperor's personal guard — all with merit.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Emperor Taizu in the assault on Ningjiang, defeated Liao troops at Dalugu City, and routed the Liao emperor's personal guard, distinguishing himself in each engagement.

sentences.zh: 遼軍來援濟州，胡石改與其兄實古乃以兵迎擊，敗之。

translations.literal: Liao troops came to relieve Jizhou; Hu Shigai and his elder brother Shigunai met them with troops and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When Liao troops came to relieve Jizhou, Hu Shigai and his elder brother Shigunai met them in battle and routed them.

sentences.zh: 還攻濟州，中流矢，戰益力，克其城。

translations.literal: Returning to attack Jizhou, he was struck by a stray arrow but fought all the harder and captured the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the renewed assault on Jizhou he was struck by an arrow but fought all the harder and took the city.

sentences.zh: 軍中稱其勇。

translations.literal: The army praised his courage.
translations.idiomatic: The army acclaimed his courage.

sentences.zh: 從攻春、泰州，降之，並降境內諸部族，其不降者皆攻拔之。

translations.literal: He followed in attacking Chun and Taizhou, reduced them, and likewise reduced the tribal groups within their borders; those who would not submit were all stormed and taken.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the assault on Chun and Taizhou, reduced both prefectures and the tribal groups within their borders, and stormed every holdout that refused to submit.

sentences.zh: 遼主西走，胡石改追至中京，獲其宮人、輜重凡八百兩。

translations.literal: The Liao emperor fled west; Hu Shigai pursued to Zhongjing and captured palace women and baggage trains totaling eight hundred cartloads.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liao emperor fled west, Hu Shigai pursued to Zhongjing and captured palace women and baggage trains totaling eight hundred cartloads.

sentences.zh: 有思泥古者，複以本部叛去，胡石改以兵五百追及之，獲其親屬部人以還。

translations.literal: One Sinigu again rebelled with his tribal group; Hu Shigai pursued with five hundred troops, overtook him, and brought back his kinsmen and tribesmen.
translations.idiomatic: When Sinigu rebelled again with his tribal group, Hu Shigai pursued with five hundred troops, overtook him, and brought back his kinsmen and followers.

sentences.zh: 德州複叛，胡石改以兵五千克其城。

translations.literal: Dezhou rebelled again; Hu Shigai took the city with five thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezhou rebelled again, Hu Shigai retook the city with five thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 從婁室擊敗敵兵二萬於歸化之南，並降歸化。

translations.literal: Following Loushi he defeated twenty thousand enemy troops south of Guihua and also reduced Guihua.
translations.idiomatic: Following Loushi he defeated twenty thousand enemy troops south of Guihua and reduced Guihua as well.

sentences.zh: 從取居庸關，並燕之屬縣及其山谷諸屯。

translations.literal: He followed in taking Juyong Pass and the subordinate counties of Yan and the various valley encampments.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the capture of Juyong Pass and the subordinate counties of Yan along with their valley encampments.

sentences.zh: 移失部既降，複叛去，胡石改引兵追及，戰敗之，俘獲甚眾。

translations.literal: The Yishi tribe had submitted but rebelled again; Hu Shigai led troops in pursuit, defeated them in battle, and captured many.
translations.idiomatic: The Yishi tribe had submitted but rebelled again; Hu Shigai pursued, defeated them in battle, and took many captives.

sentences.zh: 澤州諸部有逃者，皆追複之。

translations.literal: Among the tribes of Ze Prefecture there were fugitives; all were pursued and recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Among the tribal groups of Ze Prefecture there were fugitives; he pursued and recovered them all.

sentences.zh: 又敗叛人於臨潢，誅其酋領而安撫其人民。

translations.literal: He again defeated rebels at Linhuang, executed their chieftains, and pacified the people.
translations.idiomatic: He again defeated rebels at Linhuang, executed their chieftains, and pacified the populace.

sentences.zh: 天眷二年，遷永定軍節度使，改武定軍，徙汴京留守。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianjuan he was transferred to Military Commissioner of the Yongding Army, changed to the Wuding Army, and moved to be Defender of Bianjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianjuan (1139) he was transferred to Military Commissioner of the Yongding Army, then the Wuding Army, and finally Defender of Bianjing.

sentences.zh: 天德三年，授世襲猛安。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tiande he was granted a hereditary meng'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tiande (1145) he was granted a hereditary meng'an.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十八。

translations.literal: He died at age sixty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of sixty-eight.

sentences.zh: 宗賢，本名阿魯。

translations.literal: Zong Xian, original name Alu.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Xian, born Alu.

sentences.zh: 太祖伐遼，從攻甯江州、臨潢府。

translations.literal: When Taizu campaigned against the Liao, he followed in attacking Ningjiang Prefecture and Linhuang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizu campaigned against Liao, he joined the assaults on Ningjiang and Linhuang prefectures.

sentences.zh: 太宗監國，選侍左右，甚見親信。

translations.literal: When Taizong supervised the state, he was selected to attend at his side and was greatly trusted.
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Taizong supervised the realm as regent, Zong Xian was chosen to attend him and won his deep trust.

sentences.zh: 臨潢複叛，從宗望複取之。

translations.literal: When Linhuang rebelled again, he followed Zongwang in retaking it.
translations.idiomatic: When Linhuang rebelled again, he followed Zongwang in retaking the city.

sentences.zh: 為內庫都提點，再遷歸德軍節度使。

translations.literal: He became Chief Intendant of the Inner Treasury and was again transferred to Military Commissioner of the Guide Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Chief Intendant of the Inner Treasury and later transferred to Military Commissioner of the Guide Army.

sentences.zh: 政寬簡，境內大治。

translations.literal: His governance was lenient and simple; within his borders there was great order.
translations.idiomatic: His governance was lenient and straightforward, and the region was brought to good order.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，士民數百人相率詣朝廷請留。

translations.literal: When his term ended, several hundred gentry and commoners went together to the court to request that he remain.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended, several hundred local gentry and commoners went to court together to ask that he be kept in post.

sentences.zh: 及改武定軍，百姓扶老攜幼送數十里，悲號而去。

translations.literal: When he was changed to the Wuding Army, the people, supporting the old and leading the young, escorted him for several tens of li, weeping and wailing as they departed.
translations.idiomatic: When he was transferred to the Wuding Army command, the people escorted him for miles, old and young together, weeping as they turned back.

sentences.zh: 改永定軍。

translations.literal: He was changed to the Yongding Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the Yongding Army command.

sentences.zh: 秉德廉訪官吏，士民持盆水與鏡，前拜言曰：「使君廉明清直類此，民實賴之。」

translations.literal: Bingde was inspecting officials for integrity; gentry and commoners came forward holding basins of water and mirrors, bowing and saying: "Our commissioner is as clear and upright as these — the people truly rely on him."
translations.idiomatic: When Bingde came to inspect officials for integrity, the people came forward with basins of water and mirrors, bowed, and said, "Our commissioner is as clear and upright as these — we truly depend on him."

sentences.zh: 秉德曰：「吾聞郡僚廉能如一，汝等以為如何？」

translations.literal: Bingde said: "I have heard that the prefectural staff are all alike in integrity and ability — what do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: Bingde asked, "I have heard that the prefectural staff are all equally upright and capable — what do you think?"

sentences.zh: 眾對曰：「公勤清儉皆法則於使君耳。」

translations.literal: The crowd answered: "Their diligence, clarity, and thrift all take your commissioner as their model."
translations.idiomatic: They replied, "Their diligence, integrity, and thrift all follow your commissioner's example."

sentences.zh: 因謂宗賢曰：「人謂君善治，當在甲乙，果然賢使君也。」

translations.literal: He then said to Zong Xian: "People say you govern well and should rank among the top — truly a worthy commissioner."
translations.idiomatic: He then told Zong Xian, "People say you govern well and should rank among the best — you are indeed a worthy commissioner."

sentences.zh: 用是超遷兩階。

translations.literal: For this he was promoted two ranks beyond the norm.
translations.idiomatic: For this he was promoted two ranks beyond the norm.

sentences.zh: 天德初，授世襲謀克，馳驛召之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tiande he was granted a hereditary meng'an command and summoned by express relay.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Tiande era he was granted a hereditary meng'an command and summoned to court by express relay.

sentences.zh: 雄州父老相率張青繩懸明鏡於公署，老幼填門，三日乃得去。

translations.literal: The elders of Xiong Prefecture together stretched blue cords and hung bright mirrors at the government office; old and young filled the gates, and only after three days could he leave.
translations.idiomatic: The elders of Xiong Prefecture hung bright mirrors from blue cords at his yamen; young and old packed the gates, and he could not leave for three days.

sentences.zh: 封定國公，再除忠順軍節度使，賜以玉帶。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Duke of Ding, again appointed Military Commissioner of the Zhongshun Army, and granted a jade belt.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Duke of Ding, appointed Military Commissioner of the Zhongshun Army, and granted a jade belt.

sentences.zh: 捕盜司執數人至府，宗賢問曰：「罪狀明白否？」

translations.literal: The Office for Capturing Bandits brought several men to the prefecture; Zong Xian asked: "Are the charges clear?"
translations.idiomatic: When the Office for Capturing Bandits brought several suspects to his yamen, Zong Xian asked, "Are the charges clear?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「獄具矣。」

translations.literal: They answered: "The case is complete."
translations.idiomatic: They replied, "The case is closed."

sentences.zh: 宗賢閱其案，謂僚佐曰：「吾察此輩必冤。」

translations.literal: Zong Xian reviewed their dossiers and told his staff: "I observe that these men must be wronged."
translations.idiomatic: Zong Xian reviewed the dossiers and told his staff, "These men must have been wronged."

sentences.zh: 不數日，賊果得，人服其明。

translations.literal: Within a few days the real bandits were indeed captured, and the people admired his discernment.
translations.idiomatic: Within days the real culprits were captured, and the people admired his discernment.

sentences.zh: 改曷懶路兵馬都總管，曆廣甯尹，封廣平郡王。

translations.literal: He was changed to Commander-in-Chief of the Yalan Circuit forces, served as Prefect of Guangning, and was enfeoffed as Prince of Guangping Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Commander-in-Chief of the Yalan Circuit forces, served as Prefect of Guangning, and was enfeoffed as Prince of Guangping.

sentences.zh: 改崇義軍節度使，兼領北京宗室事。

translations.literal: He was changed to Military Commissioner of the Chongyi Army and concurrently oversaw imperial clan affairs in the Northern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Military Commissioner of the Chongyi Army with concurrent charge of imperial clan affairs in the Northern Capital.

sentences.zh: 正隆例奪王爵，加金紫光祿大夫，改臨海軍。

translations.literal: By the regulation of Zhenglong princely titles were stripped; he was given Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Blue Ribbon and changed to the Linhai Army.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhenglong regulation his princely title was stripped; he was granted Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Blue Ribbon and transferred to the Linhai Army.

sentences.zh: 大定初，遣使召之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dading envoys were sent to summon him.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Dading era envoys were sent to summon him to court.

sentences.zh: 宗賢率諸宗室見於遼陽，除同簽大宗正事，封景國公，致仕。

translations.literal: Zong Xian led the various imperial clansmen to present themselves at Liaoyang; he was appointed Associate Director of the Bureau of Imperial Clan Affairs, enfeoffed as Duke of Jing, and retired.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Xian led the imperial clansmen to present themselves at Liaoyang, was appointed Associate Director of the Bureau of Imperial Clan Affairs, enfeoffed as Duke of Jing, and retired.

sentences.zh: 起為婆速路兵馬都總管，複致仕。

translations.literal: He was recalled as Commander-in-Chief of the Basu Circuit forces and again retired.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as Commander-in-Chief of the Basu Circuit forces and retired a second time.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 特進撻懶，宗室子。

translations.literal: Special Advancement Talan, a son of the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: Talan, holder of Special Advancement and a member of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 年十六，事太祖，未嘗去左右。

translations.literal: At age sixteen he served Taizu and never left his side.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen he entered Emperor Taizu's service and never left his side.

sentences.zh: 出河店之役，太祖欲親戰，撻懶控其馬而止之曰：「主君何為輕敵。

translations.literal: At the battle of Chuhedian, Taizu wished to fight in person; Talan seized his horse and stopped him, saying: "My lord, why treat the enemy lightly?
translations.idiomatic: At the battle of Chuhedian, when Emperor Taizu wished to fight in person, Talan seized his horse and said, "My lord, why expose yourself to the enemy?

sentences.zh: 臣請效力。」

translations.literal: Your servant asks to exert his strength."
translations.idiomatic: Let your servant take the field."

sentences.zh: 即挺槍前，手殺七人。

translations.literal: He immediately levelled his spear and advanced, personally killing seven men.
translations.idiomatic: He levelled his spear and charged, killing seven men with his own hand.

sentences.zh: 已而槍折，騎士曳而下者九人。

translations.literal: Presently his spear broke; horsemen dragged nine men down from their mounts.
translations.idiomatic: When his spear broke, he dragged nine horsemen from their saddles.

sentences.zh: 太祖壯之曰：「誠得此輩數十，雖萬眾不能當也。」

translations.literal: Taizu admired him and said: "If one truly had several tens of such men, even ten thousand could not withstand them."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizu exclaimed, "With several dozen men like this, even ten thousand could not stand against us."

sentences.zh: 及戰于達魯古城，遼兵一千陣于營外，太祖遣撻懶往擊之。

translations.literal: When they fought at Dalugu City, a thousand Liao troops formed battle lines outside the camp; Taizu sent Talan to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: At the battle of Dalugu City, when a thousand Liao troops drew up outside the camp, Emperor Taizu sent Talan to attack them.

sentences.zh: 撻懶沖出敵陣，大敗其眾。

translations.literal: Talan charged through the enemy formation and routed their host.
translations.idiomatic: Talan charged through the enemy line and routed them completely.

sentences.zh: 攻臨潢府、春、泰州、中、西二京，皆有功。

translations.literal: In attacks on Linhuang Prefecture, Chun and Taizhou, and the Central and Western capitals, he had merit in all.
translations.idiomatic: He distinguished himself in the captures of Linhuang, Chun and Taizhou, and the Central and Western capitals.

sentences.zh: 天輔六年，授謀克。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianfu he was granted a meng'an command.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Tianfu (1122) he was granted a meng'an command.

sentences.zh: 天會四年，從伐宋，屢以功受賞。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianhui he followed in the campaign against Song and repeatedly received rewards for merit.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tianhui (1126) he joined the campaign against Song and was repeatedly rewarded for his service.

sentences.zh: 明年，再舉至汴。

translations.literal: The next year the campaign was raised again as far as Bian.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the armies advanced again to Bian (Kaifeng).

sentences.zh: 宗望聞宋人會諸路援兵于睢陽，遣撻懶與阿里刮將兵二千往拒之。

translations.literal: Zongwang heard that the Song were gathering relief troops from all routes at Suiyang and sent Talan with Aligua leading two thousand troops to block them.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that the Song were gathering relief armies from all routes at Suiyang, Zongwang sent Talan and Aligua with two thousand troops to block them.

sentences.zh: 敗其前鋒軍三萬於杞縣，又破三寨，擒宋京東路都總管胡直孺、南路都統制隋師元及其三將並直孺二子，遂取拱州，降寧陵。

translations.literal: He defeated their vanguard of thirty thousand at Qi County, also broke three stockades, captured the Song Eastern Route Commander-in-Chief Hu Zhiru, Southern Route Commander Sui Shiyuan and his three generals together with Zhiru's two sons, then took Gongzhou and reduced Ningling.
translations.idiomatic: He routed a Song vanguard of thirty thousand at Qi County, stormed three stockades, captured the Eastern Route Commander-in-Chief Hu Zhiru, the Southern Route Commander Sui Shiyuan and three of his generals along with Zhiru's two sons, then took Gongzhou and accepted the surrender of Ningling.

sentences.zh: 複破二萬于睢陽，進取亳州。

translations.literal: He again defeated twenty thousand at Suiyang and advanced to take Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He routed another twenty thousand at Suiyang and advanced to take Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 聞宋兵十萬且至，會宗望益兵四千，合擊，大敗之。

translations.literal: Hearing that a hundred thousand Song troops were about to arrive, he joined Zongwang's reinforcement of four thousand and together struck, inflicting a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: When word came that a hundred thousand Song troops were approaching, he joined Zongwang's four-thousand-man reinforcement and together inflicted a crushing defeat.

sentences.zh: 其卒二千，陣而立，馳之不動，即麾軍去馬擊之，盡殪，擒其將石瑱而還。

translations.literal: Two thousand of their soldiers stood in formation; charging at them they did not stir; he then ordered the army to dismount and strike them, slaughtering all, and captured their general Shi Zhen and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Two thousand Song soldiers stood firm in formation and did not break when charged; Talan ordered his men to dismount and attack on foot, slaughtered them all, captured their general Shi Zhen, and returned.

sentences.zh: 帥府嘉其功，賞賚優渥。

translations.literal: The command praised his merit and rewarded him generously.
translations.idiomatic: The field headquarters praised his achievement and rewarded him generously.

sentences.zh: 睿宗駐兵熙州，分遣諸將略地。

translations.literal: Prince Ruizong stationed troops at Xi Prefecture and dispatched the various generals to seize territory.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ruizong stationed troops at Xi Prefecture and dispatched his generals to seize territory.

sentences.zh: 撻懶以軍五百入六盤山十六寨，降其官八十餘，民戶四千，獲馬二千疋。

translations.literal: Talan with five hundred troops entered sixteen stockades of Mount Liupan, reducing more than eighty officials, four thousand households, and capturing two thousand horses.
translations.idiomatic: Talan led five hundred men into sixteen stockades on Mount Liupan, securing the submission of more than eighty officials and four thousand households and capturing two thousand horses.

sentences.zh: 皇統中，累加銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: During Huangtong he was repeatedly promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Silver Seal.
translations.idiomatic: During the Huangtong era he was repeatedly promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Silver Seal.

sentences.zh: 天德初，加特進，授世襲猛安。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tiande he was given Special Advancement and granted a hereditary meng'an.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Tiande era he was granted Special Advancement and a hereditary meng'an.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十五。

translations.literal: He died at age sixty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of sixty-five.

sentences.zh: 海陵遷諸陵於大房山，以撻懶嘗給事太祖，命作石像，置睿陵前。
